benefits: Know your true monthly cost before you visit the dealer - including tax.
See exactly how much of each payment is depreciation vs financing.
Compare lease offers side by side by changing one number at a time.
Private by design - your deal numbers never leave your browser.

faqs.a: Money factor = APR / 2400. So a 6% APR equals a money factor of 0.0025. Dealers quote money factor because it plugs directly into the lease formula; this calculator converts APR for you.
Depreciation is the biggest lever: a higher residual (say 60% vs 50% of price) directly shrinks the depreciation fee, which is usually the largest part of the payment.
faqs.q: How do I lower my lease payment?

faqs.a: Money down reduces the capitalized cost, which lowers both the depreciation and finance fees. But large down payments on leases are risky - if the car is totaled, you generally do not get that money back.
faqs.q: Should I put money down on a lease?

faqs.a: Leasing usually wins if you want a new car every 2-3 years with warranty coverage and lower monthly payments. Buying usually wins if you keep cars long-term, because you eventually own an asset.
The dealer usually offers to sell you the car at the residual value stated in the contract. Compare that price with the car's market value first - sometimes it is a bargain, sometimes not.
faqs.q: Can I buy the car at the end of the lease?

faqs.a: No. The calculation is done in your browser and nothing is stored or transmitted.

lease-calculator.formula:
Money factor = APR / 2400
Depreciation fee = (net cap cost - residual) / term months
Finance fee = (net cap cost + residual) x money factor
Monthly payment = (depreciation fee + finance fee) x (1 + tax rate)
howTo: Enter the vehicle's price (capitalized cost) and any down payment.
Enter the residual value - what the car is expected to be worth at lease end.
Enter the APR (the calculator converts it to a money factor) and the lease term in months.
Add your local sales tax rate.
Read your monthly payment, split into depreciation and finance fees, plus the total lease cost.
keyFacts: A lease payment has two parts: a depreciation fee (value you use up) and a finance fee (interest on the money tied up).
Money factor is just APR divided by 2400 - dealers use it because it plugs straight into the formula.
The residual value is set by the leasing company; a higher residual means a lower monthly payment.
You pay sales tax on the monthly payment in most US states, not on the full car price.
Typical car leases run 24 to 39 months; longer terms lower the payment but raise total cost.
Wear-and-tear and mileage-overage charges at lease end are not part of the monthly payment.
